text: Databases are organised systems for storing and managing information. Traditional relational databases use SQL and store data in tables with rows and columns. NoSQL databases, on the other hand, are more flexible and handle unstructured data well. To get information from a database, you write queries, which are instructions that ask specific questions. Before building a database, you need data modelling to plan how information connects and stays organised. Indexes are another useful feature because they help the database find data faster, just like an index in a book. Understanding these basics makes it easier to choose the right database for your needs.
